memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The commander of the Lord's army replied, "Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so. — Josh 5:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The commander's first word to Joshua is not about military tactics but about holiness: "Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy." Before any instructions about conquering Jericho, God calls Joshua to reverence. What made the ground holy was not the soil itself but the presence of God upon it. Where God is, is holy.

If these words sound familiar, they should. God spoke almost the very same words to Moses at the burning bush (Ex 3:5). This is a deliberate echo, assuring Joshua that the same holy God who commissioned Moses is now commissioning him. The God of the past is the God of the present. And it reminds us that every true encounter with God begins with reverence.

Notice the simple obedience: "And Joshua did so." No argument, no delay. He removed his sandals at once. When we truly recognise God's holy presence, the natural response is humble, immediate obedience.

We live in an age that easily treats God casually, forgetting that He is holy. Yet the closer we draw to God through Christ, the more we should hold together both intimacy and awe. Jesus has opened the way for us to come near with confidence (Heb 10:19-22), but the God we come to is still the Holy One. Let us come boldly, yes — but never carelessly. Reverence is the ground on which all obedience stands, and it is holy ground indeed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you approach God with reverence, or have you grown a little casual with Him?
2. What would "taking off your sandals" look like in your walk with God today?
3. How do you hold together both nearness to God and awe before His holiness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, forgive me when I treat You casually. Teach me to come near through Christ with both confidence and deep reverence, ready to obey at once. Amen.
